compiled_state.description:
## Why

Plan-review Pass-4 coaching is rendered per finding, so when several findings share one
root cause the author receives N instance-level fixes and no signal that the *method* is at
fault. A downstream project reported one story costing 7 review passes and ~35 blocking
findings, where the criterion distribution (`G1G2` blocking in 3 distinct passes, `E4` in 4,
`G6` in 4) traced to a single enumeration-method failure: the author kept adding the
specific file the reviewer named instead of enumerating the population that file was drawn
from, so the next pass surfaced the next unenumerated member.

The move registry's nearest existing move is `12` ("Generalize {subject} across the rest of
the work."). It is always-applicable and carries no proof obligation, so satisfying it is
still an unverifiable claim — three passes running the author asserted the enumeration was
complete when it was not. What ended the loop was an acceptance criterion in the form of a
`grep` expecting zero matches, which an incomplete enumeration cannot satisfy.

## What

Add one built-in Pass-4 coaching move that reframes a named instance as a sample from a
population and requires a machine-checkable completeness proof, scoped via `applies_when` to
the criteria where a population actually exists.

## Scope

In scope:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` — one new entry in `MOVE_REGISTRY`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the mirroring row in the move table
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — one focused test for the new move

Out of scope:

- changes to any existing move's id, name, template, or `applies_when`
- the review kernel (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/coach.py`) — mechanism is unchanged
- the code-review move registry (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py`)
- cross-pass recurrence detection, criterion-concentration coaching, and structured
  incompleteness flags — the other upstream proposals, which need new machinery
- Pass 1, Pass 2, Pass 3 behavior; criterion text; `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`

## Approach

`MOVE_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` is the plan-review gate's
catalog for the shared kernel coach mechanism. Ids `1`–`14` are taken, so add exactly:

- key `15`
- `name`: `sample, not the population`
- `template`: `Treat {subject} as one sample from a population, not a single item to fix — enumerate the whole population by the distinct ways the pattern occurs, then add a machine-checkable acceptance criterion that fails while any instance remains.`
- `applies_when`: `["G1G2", "E4", "G6", "A1"]`

The template carries exactly one `{subject}` placeholder, which
`rebar.llm.review_kernel.coach.validate_move_registry` requires at load time, and the LLM
never authors prose — `render_coach_notes` formats the locked template with a validated
bounded noun-phrase subject.

The four triggers are real criterion ids in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`
and are the criteria where a finding names a member of a population:
`G1G2` and `E4` (facet `codebase-grounding` — unenumerated consumers, unprobed assertions),
`A1` (facet `codebase-grounding` — call sites behind the rule of three), and `G6`
(facet `approach-soundness`, checklist key `mechanism_correctness` — unhandled edge/empty
cases). Verifiability criteria (`E6`, `F1`) are deliberately excluded: a missing proving
command is not a population.

Scoping via `applies_when` — rather than sharpening move `12` — keeps the change additive:
`rebar.llm.review_kernel.coach.applicable_moves` admits move `15` only when a surviving
finding's `criteria[]` intersects those four ids, so no unrelated review sees it, and move
`12` stays available for generalization findings that have no machine-checkable population.
Prior art for a scoped built-in move is move `10` (`applies_when: ["G5", "A1", "T2"]`) and
move `13` (`applies_when: ["G7"]`); prior art for a scoped coaching move added for a specific
review failure is ticket `truthful-specified-silverfish`, which used the project overlay
because its criterion was project-specific — this move's triggers are core criteria, so it
belongs in the built-in registry.

`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_move_registry_matches_docs_table` asserts the doc move
table and `MOVE_REGISTRY` have identical id sets and templates, so the new row in
`docs/plan-review-gate.md` must be added in the same change or that existing test fails.
`tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py` (the always-applicable-except-scoped assertion) already
covers move `15` generically once it declares `applies_when`.

## Dependencies

None.

## Test Strategy

Assert the new registry entry's id, name, exact template, and exact trigger set directly on
`MOVE_REGISTRY`, and assert its applicability is off with no triggers and on for each of its
four triggers via the kernel's `move_applies`. The docs-table mirror and the
scoped-applicability invariant are covered by the two existing tests named above, which run
in the same suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `MOVE_REGISTRY` contains key `15` whose `name` is `sample, not the population` and
      whose `template` is the exact sentence specified in this plan. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k population_move` — expected: passing.
- [ ] Move `15` declares exactly `["G1G2", "E4", "G6", "A1"]` in `applies_when`, is not
      applicable with an empty trigger set, and is applicable for each of those four
      triggers individually. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k population_move` — expected: passing.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md`'s move table mirrors the new entry, and no existing move's
      template changed. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k "move_registry" tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py -k move` — expected: passing.
- [ ] No existing move id, name, template, or `applies_when` changed. Prove with
      `git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py | grep -c '^-'` —
      expected output: `0` (the diff is addition-only).
- [ ] The full plan-review and review-kernel suites are green. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py` — expected: passing.
- [ ] Lint and typecheck pass. Prove with `make lint && make typecheck` — expected: exit 0.
